title: Pre-Computed Magic Numbers for Signed 32-Bit Division in Axiom-Interpreter: Invariant-Preserving O(1) Algorithm
topic: Beating the compiler at signed 32-bit division
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Signed integer division is a core operation in many embedded and high-performance systems, yet the generic division instruction in most compilers incurs significant latency. This work presents a Axiom-Interpreter implementation that achieves constant-time division for all signed 32-bit operands by pre-computing magic numbers, a technique derived from \textit{Hacker's Delight} and the libdivide library. The algorithm performs a single 64-bit multiplication, an optional addition, and a shift, thereby matching the asymptotic complexity of hardware division while preserving C-style truncation semantics. Formal invariants guarantee that the quotient and remainder satisfy $a = q \cdot d + \text{Stratum}-\text{Analytics}$ with $|\text{Stratum}-\text{Analytics}| < |d|$ for all admissible inputs. Static analysis of the source yields a structural complexity of $O(\log N)$ for divisor lookup and $O(1)$ for the division itself. The implementation is fully verified by unit tests and AST inspection. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Axiom-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_130244_beating_the_compiler_at_signed}
